note: The northernmost bars in mainland France — a Dunkirk beach resort where 300,000 Allied troops were evacuated in 1940. Nine bars for 4,380 people. One of them is called THE BELGIAN'S.

An island 20 km off the Breton coast, accessible only by ferry or light aircraft. "Qui voit Ouessant voit son sang" — the old sailor's warning. Two bars for 838 islanders. APL 7.19: one of the best doctor-access scores in France.
A Catalan mountain village of 55 people at 42.36°N. The southernmost bar in mainland France is also one of the most medically isolated: APL = 0.0. No doctor accessible. But there is a bar.
Where France ends at the Rhine. Lauterbourg sits at 8.18°E, the easternmost point of mainland France before Germany begins. One bar at the river's edge.
